record.official_vs_impostor_test: An account is OFFICIAL for a company iff (check1 OR check2.satisfied) holds -- name alone is NEVER sufficient, because a fan account, a parody or an unrelated same-name entity all pass a name match. check1: the company's own measured web presence (its ir_domain once AMGT-s-4/-b4 resolve one, or a one-pager already on file) LINKS to the account by its exact platform URL -- this already establishes the company's own identity, so check1 alone is sufficient. check2 is TYPED, never a bare boolean (VerificationMark(present, identity_bound)): `present` -- the platform's own verification mark is present on the account at read time -- and `identity_bound` -- the mark attests THIS company's own identity, not merely that the account is 'verified' in some platform-generic sense -- are SEPARATE facts, and check2.satisfied requires BOTH (AMGT-rb-15, round 2b, fixes AMGT-r-15's C-S14 FAIL: a non-identity-bound verification mark plus a copied bio previously still passed because check2 was untyped and any truthy value counted). A mark present but NOT identity-bound is NOT check2 -- it resolves exactly as if no mark were present. check3: the account's own bio/description names the company's registered domain, checked by the SAME display_link-vs-link discipline the SOURCE rule enforces (lib/research/rules/source.py: match the domain, never a display name or an obfuscated redirect) -- the WEAKEST and most forgeable of the three. THE AND-CLAUSE (AMGT-r-15, round 2, fixes AMGT-s-15's AC6 FAIL: the prior bare-OR let a copied 'official account of <domain>' bio admit on check3 ALONE): check3 must CO-OCCUR with check1 OR a satisfied check2 to count toward OFFICIAL at all -- on its own, or alongside an identity-blind check2, it is NOT sufficient; it may only STRENGTHEN a result that already has check1 or a satisfied check2 True, never supply admission alone. Formally: official := check1 OR check2.satisfied; check3 alone (check1 False and check2 not satisfied) does NOT admit -- it is refused as not-official, never official on the forgeable check by itself, and never official merely because a verification mark is present without being identity-bound. Any handle entry graduating past UNRESOLVED carries which check(s) it satisfied, in its own `evidence` field -- absent that, it is INFERRED, never MEASURED. Predicate: lib/research/lists/impostor.py:evaluate_official_vs_impostor(check1, check2, check3) applies this rule without re-derivation; check2 is a VerificationMark, not a bare boolean -- passing one raises TypeError.
